history.heading: First European colony
paragraphs: The Dominican Republic occupies the eastern two-thirds of the island of Hispaniola, which it shares with Haiti. The Taíno inhabited the island when Columbus arrived in 1492. Santo Domingo, founded in 1496, is the oldest permanent European city in the Americas, with the first cathedral, university and hospital in the New World; its colonial zone is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The Taíno population was nearly wiped out within decades. The colony declined as Spain focused on Mexico and Peru, and in 1697 the western part of the island became the French colony of Saint-Domingue, later Haiti.

history.heading: Independence
paragraphs: After a period of Haitian rule from 1822 to 1844, the Dominican Republic declared independence on 27 February 1844. Spain briefly re-annexed the country from 1861 to 1865. The United States occupied it from 1916 to 1924.

history.heading: Trujillo and democracy
paragraphs: Rafael Trujillo ruled as a brutal dictator from 1930 until his assassination in 1961. In 1937 his forces massacred thousands of Haitians along the border. After a US intervention in 1965, Joaquín Balaguer governed for long periods with authoritarian methods.
Since the 1990s the country has had regular democratic elections and peaceful transfers of power.

culture.heading: Music and baseball
paragraphs: Dominican culture blends Spanish, African and Taíno heritage. Spanish is the official language, and most people are Catholic. Merengue and bachata, both recognised by UNESCO, are the national music and dance genres, with famous artists such as Juan Luis Guerra.

Baseball is a passion, and the Dominican Republic has produced a large number of Major League Baseball players. La bandera dominicana (rice, beans and meat) is the national dish, and mangú is a favourite breakfast.

politics.heading: Presidential republic
paragraphs: The Dominican Republic is a presidential republic with a president elected for four years and a bicameral Congress. The Modern Revolutionary Party has governed since 2020.
Relations with Haiti are a major political issue, including border security, migration and the deportation of Haitian migrants, and the citizenship of people of Haitian descent.

economy.heading: Fast-growing economy
paragraphs: The Dominican Republic has been one of the fastest-growing economies in Latin America for decades. Tourism is the leading sector, with resorts such as Punta Cana attracting millions of visitors. Free trade zones produce medical devices, clothing and cigars, and the country exports gold, cocoa, bananas and tobacco.
Remittances from the large Dominican diaspora in the United States are important. The currency is the Dominican peso. Inequality and informal work remain challenges.
